# Side-by-side check against the real xfig (W22)

**Status:** 2026-10-25, first report: 97 scenarios, none failed to run; round 2 (below): 119 more scenarios, none failed to run. Generated by `cargo xtask xfig-compare` (see [development.md](development.md)); the HTML with the images is `target/xfig-compare/index.html` (not committed, regenerate it). Reviewed by reading the worst-scoring and one image of each kind of scenario; the `.fig` object differences are complete for the scenarios that save.

**Setup:** real xfig 3.2.9a (`/opt/homebrew/bin/xfig`, default options, scratch `HOME`) headless on `Xvfb :77`, window 1400x1000, zoom 1.0 (80 px/in); RustFig 1400 pt wide at zoom 1, light theme, Fig (0,0) at the canvas corner. Clicks are snapped to 1/16 inch (75 Fig units) so both apps' pixel origins give the same Fig point. The RustFig window is clipped to the screen height (826 pt on the test Mac), so its bottom bar sits higher than xfig's; scores for the whole window therefore start at about 0.23 and for the canvas crop at about 0.08 for any scenario (layout, background, antialiasing): compare scores between scenarios, not with zero.

**Method:** each scenario selects a mode (xfig: mouse on the mode button as in `w_modepanel.c`'s grid, RustFig: its accessible label), clicks the same Fig points, screenshots both, and where it changes the drawing saves both `.fig` files. Text height/length are not compared (fonts), nor xfig's radius -1 against 0 on non-box polylines.

**Coverage this round:** all 40 mode buttons selected (message, mouse-button hints, indicator panel); one object drawn with each drawing mode except picture and library (dialogs only); move, copy, delete, flip up/down and left/right, rotate cw/ccw, scale, move/add/delete point, update, convert, add arrow, and the edit panel of a box, circle, polyline and text; the five menus open; the pop-ups of line width, style, fill style, pen/fill colour, depth, join, cap, grid, point position, zoom, arrow mode/type/size, text justification/angle/flags/size/font. Round 2 covers the second-level menu entries and dialogs behind them, compounds, align, join/split, chop, tangent, measure, picture objects, text editing keys and the middle/right buttons. Still not covered: Shift/Ctrl variants, other fixtures (arrows, fills, splines, metric), scroll, and the Library placement (xfig has no library loaded).

## Differences

**intended** = a modern alternative CLAUDE.md allows or a decision recorded elsewhere; **real** = RustFig should change (task id proposed; `W22-n` are new rows to add to `docs/plan.md` when taken up).

### Drawn and edited objects (`.fig` output)

| # | Difference | Seen in | Verdict | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Interpolated splines are written with shape factor -1; xfig uses -0.5 (`object.h`: `S_SPLINE_INTERP`). ### Not a difference

Flip up/down and left/right, copy, delete, update, move/add/delete point and add arrow give the same `.fig` objects in both apps; box, circle, polyline, spline, polygon, arc and text drawn with the default attributes give the same coordinates (after snapping) and attributes; the five menus have xfig's entries in xfig's order; the Snap menu is identical.

## Round 2 (2026-10-25)

**Coverage:** 119 more scenarios on a second fixture (`FIXTURE2`: a compound of box and circle, two lines to join, a four-point line to split with a line crossing it, a polygon, an approximated spline, an arc, two texts, a picture `pic.png`, a compound of two boxes), all of them ran. Dialogs behind the menu entries (File Open, Merge, Save As, Export, Print; Edit Paste with an empty buffer, Search/Replace, Spell check, Global settings, Set units, Delete All; View Manage Styles, Zoom In, Zoom to Fit, Character map, line lengths, vertex numbers; Help About), compounds (glue by tag and by region, break and break-and-tag, open and keep visible, move/copy/delete/flip/rotate/scale/update/edit panel on a compound, move inside an open compound and close it), align (compound and canvas), join and split (vertex and segment), chop (axe, clear), tangent and normal (spline, arc), the four measure modes with their message texts, picture objects (move, copy, delete, flip, rotate, scale, update, edit panel), text editing keys (arrows, Home, End, Backspace, Return, Ctrl-A/B/D/E/F/K/W, middle and right button on empty canvas), the middle and right buttons of every editing mode (scale, move, copy, delete, update, flip, rotate, convert, add arrow, move/add/delete point, edit) and of box, circle, arc, polyline and spline drawing, the mouse-function box and message panel in every state of 23 operations (`hint-*`: start, over an object, after the first click, after the right button), the zoom keys z and Shift-Z. 78 scenarios save a figure and compare the `.fig` files: 38 are equal after the same steps, 13 change the figure in neither app (panels, measure modes), 23 differ as listed below, and 4 differ only because nothing was drawn (RustFig always writes its figure, xfig does not save an unchanged one) or because xfig sampled the synthetic mouse path as a freehand line (middle button as first point of a polyline: not comparable).

**Not comparable:** Trim and extend (xfig has no such mode), library placement (xfig's Library dialog says "None Loaded" without a library folder), drawing a picture (xfig opens its Edit panel after the second corner, RustFig the operating system's file dialog, which the check does not drive), and the file dialogs of Open, Merge and Save As (native in RustFig). xfig does not save an unchanged figure and does not save while a compound is open; scenarios that need a `.fig` close the compound first.

**Driving notes** (for the next round): the middle button of Scale (about centre), Move and Move point is a press that starts the operation and a second middle click that places; the Delete and Glue regions by the middle button are two middle clicks (corner, final corner), a press-drag-release does the same in both apps for Glue and is ignored by both for Delete; middle in Polyline mode starts a freehand line, it does not end the line; xfig's menu entries are 16 px apart below the menu button (File: New, Open, Merge, Save, Save As, Export, Print, Exit from y 34).

|---|---|---|---|---|

Zoom to Fit gives 1.33 where xfig gives 1.50 (RustFig's canvas is smaller; not counted). | dlg-view-zoom-in, dlg-view-zoom-in-click, key-zoom-out, key-shift-z | **real** | W22-16: step √2 with xfig's rounding to 1.41, 2, 2.82, 4, 5.65, 8, 11.3 (the sequence in `inc_zoom`/`dec_zoom`) |

Counts after round 2: 44 differences listed (24 in round 1, 20 in round 2), 30 real and 14 intended. Of the real ones 15 are fixed (W22-1…12, 14, 15 in round 1, W22-29 now) and 15 are open: W22-13 and W22-16…28, 30.
